abs(x).description: Returns the absolute value of a number, removing any negative sign.

add(x, y, filter = false), x + y.description: Adds two or more inputs element wise. Set filter=true to treat NaNs as 0 before summing.

densify(x).description: Converts a grouping field of many buckets into lesser number of only available buckets so as to make working with grouping fields computationally efficient

divide(x, y), x / y.description: Returns x divided by y (x / y). Note: dividing by zero raises an error; to avoid it, use divide(x, add(y, 0.0001)); adding a small epsilon to the denominator prevents divide-by-zero errors.

inverse(x).description: Returns the reciprocal of x (1 / x). Note: errors when x = 0; to avoid it, use inverse(add(x, 0.0001)); adding a small epsilon prevents divide-by-zero errors.

log(x).description: Calculates the natural logarithm of the input value. Commonly used to transform data that has positive values.

max(x, y, ..).description: Maximum value of all inputs. At least 2 inputs are required

min(x, y ..).description: Minimum value of all inputs. At least 2 inputs are required

multiply(x ,y, ... , filter=false), x *.description: Multiplies two or more inputs element wise. Set filter=true to treat NaNs as 1 before multiplication

power(x, y).description: Returns x raised to the power of y (x ^ y). Note: power(x, y) can drop the sign of x when y is non-integer; use signed_power(x, y) to preserve the sign of x.

sign(x).description: Returns the sign of a number: +1 for positive, -1 for negative, and 0 for zero. If the input is NaN, returns NaN.

signed_power(x, y).description: x raised to the power of y such that final result preserves sign of x

sqrt(x).description: Returns the non-negative square root of x. Equivalent to power(x, 0.5).

subtract(x, y, filter=false), x - y.description: Subtracts inputs left to right: x ? y ? … Supports two or more inputs. Set filter=true to treat NaNs as 0 before subtraction.

to_nan(x, value=0, reverse=false).description: Convert value to NaN or NaN to value if reverse=true

and(input1, input2).description: Returns 1 ('true') if both inputs are 1 ('true'). Otherwise, returns 0 ('false').

if_else(input1, input2, input 3).description: The if_else operator returns one of two values based on a condition. If the condition is true, it returns the first value; if false, it returns the second value.

input1 < input2.description: Returns 1 ('true') if input1 is a smaller than input2. Otherwise, returns 0 ('false').

input1 <= input2.description: Returns 1 ('true') if input1 is a smaller or the same as input2. Otherwise, returns 0 ('false').

input1 == input2.description: Returns 1 ('true') if input1 and input2 are the same. Otherwise, returns 0 ('false').

input1 > input2.description: Returns 1 ('true') if input1 is a larger than input2. Otherwise, returns 0 ('false').

input1 >= input2.description: Returns 1 ('true') if input1 is a larger or the same as input2. Otherwise, returns 0 ('false').

input1!= input2.description: Returns 1 ('true') if input1 and input2 are different numbers. Otherwise, returns 0 ('false').

not(x).description: Returns the logical negation of x. Returns 0 when x is 1 (‘true’) and 1 when x is 0 (‘false’).

or(input1, input2).description: Returns 1 if either input is true (either input1 or input2 has a value of 1), otherwise it returns 0.

days_from_last_change(x).description: Calculates the number of days since the last change in the value of a given variable.

hump(x, hump = 0.01).description: Limits amount and magnitude of changes in input (thus reducing turnover)

jump_decay(x, d, sensitivity=0.5, force=.description: If there is a huge jump in current data compare to previous one, apply force.

kth_element(x, d, k, ignore=“NaN”).description: Returns the K-th value from a time series by looking back over a specified number of (‘d’) days, with the option to ignore certain values.

last_diff_value(x, d).description: Returns the most recent value of x from the past d days that is different from the current value of x.

ts_arg_max(x, d).description: Returns the number of days since the maximum value occurred in the last d days of a time series.

ts_arg_min(x, d).description: Returns the number of days since the minimum value occurred in a time series over the past d days.

ts_av_diff(x, d).description: Calculates the difference between a value and its mean over a specified period, ignoring NaN values in the mean calculation.

ts_backfill(x,lookback = d, k=1).description: Replaces missing (NaN) values in a time series with the most recent valid value from a specified lookback window.

ts_corr(x, y, d).description: Calculates the Pearson correlation between two variables, x and y, over the past d days.

ts_count_nans(x ,d).description: Counts the number of missing (NaN) values in a data series over a specified number of days.

ts_covariance(y, x, d).description: Calculates the covariance between two time-series variables, y and x, over the past d days.

ts_decay_linear(x, d, dense = false).description: Applies a linear decay to time-series data over a set number of days, smoothing the data by averaging recent values.

ts_delay(x, d).description: Returns the value of a variable x from d days ago.

ts_delta(x, d).description: Calculates the difference between a value and its delayed version over a specified period.

ts_max(x, d).description: Returns max value of x for the past d days

ts_mean(x, d).description: Calculates the simple average (mean) value of a variable x over the past d days.

ts_min(x, d).description: Returns min value of x for the past d days

ts_product(x, d).description: Returns the product of the values of x over the past d days.

ts_quantile(x,d, driver=\"gaussian\" ).description: Calculates the ts_rank of the input and transforms it using the inverse cumulative distribution function of a specified probability distribution.

ts_rank(x, d, constant = 0).description: Ranks the value of a variable for each instrument over a specified number of past days, returning the rank of the current value.

ts_regression(y, x, d, lag = 0, rettype.description: Fits an OLS linear regression of dependent variable y on independent variable x over d days, using valid (x, y) tuples. lag defaults to 0 and optionally selects lagged regression. rettype selects: 0 = error term (residual, default); 1 = y-intercept (alpha); 2 = slope (beta); 3 = y-estimate; 4 = sum of squares of error (SSE); 5 = sum of squares of total (SST); 6 = R-square; 7 = mean square error (MSE); 8 = standard error of beta; 9 = standard error of alpha. Regressing on ts_step(1) with rettype=2 measures a time trend slope; rettype=0 returns the error term relative to the fitted trend.
ts_regression(y, x, d, lag = 0, rettype.documentation_provenance: BRAIN operator documentation supplied by the user on 2026-10-03.

ts_scale(x, d, constant = 0).description: Scales a time series to a 0–1 range based on its minimum and maximum values over a specified period.

ts_std_dev(x, d).description: Calculates the standard deviation of a data series x over the past d days.

ts_step(1).description: Returns a counter of days, incrementing by one each day.

ts_sum(x, d).description: Sum values of x for the past d days.

ts_target_tvr_decay(x, lambda_min=0, lam.description: Tune "ts_decay" to have a turnover equal to a certain target.

ts_target_tvr_delta_limit(x, y, lambda_m.description: Tune "ts_delta_limit" to have a turnover equal to a certain target.

ts_zscore(x, d).description: Calculates the Z-score of a time series, showing how far today's value is from the recent average.

normalize(x, useStd = false, limit = 0.0.description: Centers a daily cross section by subtracting the market mean; optionally divide by the cross sectional standard deviation and clamp the result.

quantile(x, driver = gaussian, sigma = 1.description: Ranks and shifts a vector of Alpha values, then applies a chosen statistical distribution to reduce outliers.

rank(x, rate=2).description: Ranks the values of the input x among all instruments, returning numbers evenly spaced between 0.0 and 1.0.

scale(x, scale=1, longscale=1, shortscal.description: Scales the input so that the sum of absolute values across all instruments equals a specified book size.

scale_down(x,constant=0).description: Scales all values in each day proportionately between 0 and 1 such that minimum value maps to 0 and maximum value maps to 1.

vector_neut(x, y).description: For given vectors x and y, it finds a new vector x* (output) such that x* is orthogonal to y

winsorize(x, std=4).description: Winsorize limits values in a data to within a specified number of standard deviations from the mean.

zscore(x).description: Z-score is a numerical measurement that describes a value's relationship to the mean of a group of values in terms of standard deviations.

vec_avg(x).description: Calculates the mean (average) of all elements in a vector field for each instrument and date.

vec_count(x).description: Number of elements in vector field x

vec_max(x).description: Maximum value form vector field x

vec_min(x).description: Minimum value form vector field x

vec_range(x).description: Difference between maximum and minimum element in vector field x

vec_stddev(x).description: Standard Deviation of vector field x

vec_sum(x).description: Calculates the sum of all values in a vector field.

bucket(rank(x), range=...).description: The bucket operator creates custom groups by dividing data into buckets (ranges) based on ranked values of any data field.

trade_when(x, y, z).description: The trade_when operator changes Alpha values only when a specific condition is met, keeps previous values otherwise, and can close positions by assigning NaN.

group_backfill(x, group, d, std = 4.0).description: Fills missing (NaN) values for instruments within the same group by calculating a winsorized mean of all non-NaN values over the past d days.

group_cartesian_product(g1, g2).description: Merge two groups into one group.

group_max(x, group).description: Maximum of x for all instruments in the same group.

group_mean(x, weight, group).description: Calculates the harmonic mean of a data field within each specified group.

group_min(x, group).description: All elements in group equals to the min value of the group.

group_neutralize(x, group).description: Neutralizes Alpha values within each specified group by subtracting the group mean from each value.

group_rank(x, group).description: Ranks each element within its group based on the input field, assigning a value between 0.0 and 1.0.

group_scale(x, group).description: Normalizes values within each group to a range between 0 and 1, making data comparable across different groups.

group_zscore(x, group).description: Calculates the Z-score of each value within its group, showing how far each value is from the group mean in terms of standard deviations.
